title: Lift-Out Technique for Ultra-Thin Plan-View Lamella Preparation Using Focused Ion Beam
content: Conventional transmission electron microscopy (TEM) sample preparation typically focuses on cross-sectional specimens, whereas plan-view lift-out techniques are less common [1, 2]. However, plan-view lift-out is critical because it allows for direct observation of a sample’s surface features and thin film interfaces—an essential advantage for layered or sandwich structures. Despite this benefit, most plan-view lift-out techniques are applied to the surface of bulk samples (typically hundreds of nanometers thick) that remain uniform. Very recently, Ghosh et al. demonstrated the preparation of a high-quality TEM plan-view sample from a multilayer structure using focused ion beam (FIB) techniques [3]. However, their multilayer structure was not laterally cross-sectional and had a scale on the order of hundreds of nanometers. To investigate the microstructural properties of ferroelectric (FE) films, including grain size and domain wall morphology, a plan-view lamella preparation process is essential for imaging thinner films with smaller grains. While Zhong et al. demonstrated plan-view sample preparation for HZO on an LSMO/STO substrate [4], no studies have focused on HZO deposited on Si. In this paper, we demonstrate how to prepare a plan-view lift-out from a 10 nm thick region in a cross-sectional sandwich structure (Au-Pd/HZO (10 nm)/Si) within a semiconductor device. Retrieving the lateral information in such thin region enables a detailed examination of grain distribution and ferroelectric domain configurations that are critical for optimizing device performance.
